title: Method to Improve Critical Current Density Measurement of Superconducting Materials
author: Shao, Liu, et al.

steps.title: Assemble double‑sided measurement system
steps.instruction: Connect the lock‑in amplifier, signal generator, power amplifier, protective resistance, non‑inductive shunt, drive coil, pick‑up coil, computer, digital multimeter, refrigerator (or liquid nitrogen bath), and all cables according to the circuit diagram shown in Fig. 1.

steps.title: Place coils and sample
steps.instruction: Mount the drive coil and the pick‑up coil on opposite sides of the superconducting film so that the film is sandwiched between them at a 0.4 mm gap from each coil; secure the coils with the cylinder holder, ensuring only the centre cylinder contains a coil (Fig. 3).

steps.title: Cool sample to transition temperature
steps.instruction: Bring the sample temperature to the superconducting phase‑transition point (78 K) using a refrigerator or by immersing the assembly in liquid nitrogen; confirm the sample is fully superconducting before proceeding.

steps.title: Optional calibration with known Jc sample
steps.instruction: If the device has been re‑configured, calibrate it by measuring a reference sample of known critical current density (e.g., obtained by a four‑probe method) following the same measurement steps.

steps.title: Select measurement range and configure electronics
steps.instruction: Set the signal‑generator output frequency between 200 Hz and 2000 Hz and adjust the digital multimeter voltage range to 1 × 10⁻⁵ V – 1 × 10⁻¹ V. For high‑performance samples or long acquisition times, cool the protective resistance and shunt resistance R0. Configure the lock‑in amplifier to separate Channel A (fundamental voltage V1) and the third‑harmonic voltage V3 at the same frequency.

substeps.instruction: Program lock‑in to output V1 (Channel A) and V3 (third harmonic).

steps.title: Acquire V1 and V3 and compute I0
steps.instruction: Measure the fundamental voltage V1 and the third‑harmonic voltage V3; calculate the drive current I0 as I0 = V1 / (2 R0) and the ordinate value as V3 / (2 f). Plot V3 / (2 f) versus I0 to obtain the third‑harmonic diagram (Fig. 4).

steps.title: Determine critical current and Jc
steps.instruction: Select a voltage‑time criterion for the phase transition (e.g., 0.2 μV·sec); read the corresponding current Ic0 from the diagram; compute the critical current density as Jc = Ic0 × k, where the proportionality factor k is obtained from calibration (k = Jc* / Ic0*).
